title: Extract policy adapters and reduce hotpath coupling in routing core
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: The current smart routing core mixes policy decision logic, fallback sequencing, and region affinity heuristics inside a single hotpath module. This causes several problems: (1) high cognitive load when making behavior changes, (2) difficulty testing fallback permutations, (3) hotpath allocations and locks that increase p95 routing latency, and (4) fast regressions when we upgrade dependencies or introduce new policy types.

Goal: Break the routing policy core into small, well-defined 'policy adapter' interfaces and a thin coordinator that composes adapters at runtime. Move fallback sequencing into a testable policy adapter with a deterministic state machine. Remove global locks and reduce per-request allocations on the hotpath. Deliver measurable p95/p99 latency improvements and better test coverage for fallback combos.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Kickoff: scoped to adapter interface, fallback adapter implementation, and coordinator rewrite. Decision: adapters will be plain interfaces with immutable config blobs pulled from the policy store. We avoid dynamic codegen for now to keep rollout safe.

2025-02-18 — Spike results: implemented prototype that extracts region affinity logic into RegionAdapter. Microbenchmarks show the coordinator-only hotpath allocations dropped by ~48% and single-threaded throughput +18%.

2025-02-24 — Design review notes from Priya Patel (PM): prefer config-driven fallback ordering to avoid ad-hoc code branches. Lucia Moreno (SRE) requested observability hooks per adapter stage — added tracing spans and token/latency tags.

2025-03-01 — PR feedback (ENG backend review): avoid allocating new fallback chain structs per request; use an arena and reuse pool across requests. Also suggested making adapter instantiation lazy to reduce memory impact of rarely used policy types.

2025-03-03 — Canary prepared: canary config created for test routes. Rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on error_rate > 0.5% or latency regressions (p95 > +15% over baseline).
acceptance_criteria: Adapter interfaces defined and documented in code and Confluence
Coordinator composes adapters and preserves existing routing behavior for current policies
Fallback sequencing moved into a testable adapter with unit tests covering edge cases (capacity loss, incompatible model variants, region failover)
Hotpath allocations reduced: p95 routing evaluation latency reduced by >=25% on synthetic traffic compared to current main
No customer-visible regressions during 2-week canary (monitoring: per-route error rate, p95/p99 latency, cost per token estimate)
Observability: adapter-level traces and metrics emitted and wired into Console dashboards
notes: Trade-offs: extracting adapters increases indirection which can add a small constant to cold-start path. Mitigation: instantiate common adapters at startup and use a small pool for ephemeral ones.
Performance note: initial benchmarks show p95 down from 14ms to ~9.8ms on the coordinator path for our control route set. After allocation pooling further improvements expected to 7.5ms p95.
QA plan: create synthetic workload in staging that exercises complex fallback trees and cross-region failures. Record deterministic inputs for eval harness.
Rollout checklist: feature flag gate, canary traffic, smoke tests (latency, error rate), post-canary retrospective to capture learnings and decide on full rollout cadence.
Related incidents: INCIDENT-2024-11-06 highlighted complex fallback loops during region flapping; this refactor should make those sequences explicit and easier to guard against.
